title: Semrush and Ahrefs alternative: SEO that also publishes
author: Cryptool
excerpt_html: SEO suites are research tools. They produce a list of things to do, and the list is only worth what your team has time to act on.
content_html:
Semrush and Ahrefs are the best research tools in SEO and nothing here disputes that. They are also, structurally, tools that produce work rather than do it. You get keyword gaps, backlink profiles, competitor analysis and a site audit with two hundred issues ranked by severity, and then somebody has to write the pages and fix the issues. For a small crypto team, that somebody does not exist. GTM runs the SEO work as well as identifying it, and it comes with your Cryptool account.

What Semrush and Ahrefs do well

Enormous crawled indexes and genuinely excellent data. Ahrefs' backlink index is the reference point in the industry and its keyword tooling is superb. Semrush is broader, covering paid search, competitor advertising research, position tracking and content optimisation. If you have an SEO specialist, these are the tools they will ask for, and they should get them.

The gap between knowing and doing

A keyword gap report is a list of pages you have not written. A site audit is a list of fixes nobody has scheduled. The research is real value, but it converts into results only through execution capacity, and execution capacity is exactly what a small team does not have. This is why so many subscriptions to these tools go unused after the first month: the dashboard was never the bottleneck.

There is also the paid side. Running search ads well is a continuous job of testing copy, managing negatives and watching spend. Research tools will tell you what competitors are bidding on; they will not run your account.

What GTM does

SEO and SEA are run, not just reported. Search engine optimisation and search engine advertising are part of what the app does continuously, rather than a report you receive and act on later.

Content is produced and published. The pages and posts that SEO depends on get written and published on-brand across your channels, which closes the loop that a research tool leaves open.

Mentions are tracked. You find out where your brand is being discussed, which is both a reputation matter and a source of the relationships that earn links.

It connects to the commercial side. Outreach, sales and partnership motions sit in the same system, so visibility leads somewhere rather than being measured for its own sake.

It is continuous. The reason most small teams fail at SEO is not a bad strategy, it is that the work stops. An always-on system does not have busy weeks.

Choosing between them

If you have an SEO specialist, or an agency doing the work, give them Ahrefs or Semrush. The data is better than anything an execution tool will show you and they will use it properly. If you have nobody, a research subscription will produce a list that grows faster than it shrinks, and you are better served by something that does the work. Some teams run both, using the research tools to check outcomes independently, which is a reasonable way to keep an execution system honest.

Common questions

Does GTM replace keyword research tools?

Not on data depth. Ahrefs and Semrush have crawled indexes that an execution product does not attempt to match. GTM is aimed at the doing rather than the researching.

Does GTM run search ads as well as organic SEO?

Yes, search engine advertising is part of what it covers alongside optimisation.

How long does SEO take to show results?

Months, in most cases, and anyone promising otherwise is selling something. The argument for an always-on tool is precisely that consistency over months is what a small team cannot sustain manually.

Can I see what it is doing?

Yes, you set up the brand and channels and the work runs from that setup.

Where do I start?

Open GTM with your Cryptool account and set up your brand.
